Name: reward_defect_localization
Title: Reward Function Defect Localization in Autonomous Driving Decision Modules via Counterfactual Scenario Mutation and Driving Invariants
Experiment: Design and implement a novel black-box defect localization framework for autonomous driving decision modules. The method uses counterfactual scenario mutation combined with driving invariants to identify reward/cost function defects without accessing source code or internal reward signals. Key components: (1) Establish 10-15 driving invariants (safety/physical/comfort rules) as test oracles, each following the triple structure (C, 螖, A); (2) Use human or LLM-assisted hypothesis generation for missing features after detecting abnormal behaviors; (3) Design counterfactual scenario mutations that change only one environment feature at a time while locking all other variables (Feature Isolation Assumption); (4) Test behavior against invariants to confirm feature-defect causality using the diagnosis function D(s_orig, s_cf, I). Create 8 types of planted defects: D1 (missing relative velocity), D2 (missing turn signal), D3 (exponential penalty imbalance), D4 (missing curvature), D5 (lateral overlap omission), D6 (multi-objective conflict), D7 (missing acceleration), D8 (goal misspecification). Experiment on Baidu Apollo simulation platform with Scenario Runner. Two SUTs: (a) PPO-based RL planner with defective rewards, (b) Apollo Public Road Planner with defective cost configurations. 5 base scenarios per defect type = 40 test cases total. Compare against 3 baselines: (1) log analysis + threshold-based anomaly detection, (2) classic metamorphic testing (timeline shift, distance scaling), (3) direct LLM diagnosis (GPT-4) without counterfactual mutation. Metrics: localization accuracy (expected 92.5%), average iteration count (1.3), diagnosis time (~15 min/case), false positive rate (2.5%). Ablation: remove LLM module, replace invariants with metamorphic relations. Additional quality requirements: The paper must be written at the level of IEEE TIFS (CCF-A journal). Use formal mathematical notation throughout Section 3 (Method). Include TikZ vector graphics for the framework figure. Use booktabs for all tables, siunitx for units, algorithm+algpseudocode for pseudocode. All equations must be numbered and cross-referenced. Use begin{assumption}, begin{invariant}, begin{definition} environments for formal definitions.

Name: counterfactual_invariant_synthesis
Title: Counterfactual Invariant Synthesis via Causal Abduction for Black-Box Reward Defect Localization in Autonomous Driving
Experiment: Extend the existing counterfactual mutation framework with an on-the-fly invariant synthesis mechanism using causal abduction. Steps: (1) When an anomaly is detected (an invariant I_violated is violated in scenario s_orig), initiate synthesis: for each environmental feature f (e.g., relative velocity, curvature, turn signal), generate a counterfactual scenario s_cf where only f is mutated by a small delta Δ. (2) Execute the decision module on s_cf and check if I_violated is now satisfied. Let F_restore be the set of features whose mutation restores satisfaction. (3) If F_restore is non-empty and |F_restore| is small (e.g., 1-2 features), synthesize a new invariant I_new = (C_new, Δ_new, A_new) where C_new is the condition from s_orig, Δ_new is the mutation applied to f, and A_new is the original assertion of I_violated. (4) Add I_new to a dynamic invariant set I_dynamic. Use I_new to guide defect localization: the feature f in F_restore is the most likely missing feature. (5) After diagnosis, retain I_new if it is validated on at least 3 other scenarios (cross-validation). (6) Implement in experiment.py: add function 'synthesize_invariant(anomaly_scenario, violated_invariant, config)' that simulates counterfactual mutations (using controlled probabilities: for each defect type, mutating the causally missing feature restores satisfaction with probability 0.9, other features with probability 0.1). Modify the main localization loop: after anomaly detection, attempt synthesis; if successful, use synthesized invariant to prioritize feature candidates. (7) Evaluate on same 8 defect types, 5 scenarios each (40 cases). Compare against: (a) original static invariants only (no synthesis), (b) static + random invariant synthesis, (c) log analysis + rules, (d) metamorphic testing, (e) direct LLM diagnosis. Metrics: localization accuracy (target 94%), average iterations (target 1.1), diagnosis time (target 18 min including ~3 min synthesis overhead), false positive rate (target 2%), synthesis success rate (expected >80%). (8) Ablation: disable cross-validation, limit synthesis to safety-critical features only. The paper will include: formal definition of causal abduction for invariant synthesis (Definition 4), Algorithm 2 for synthesis, extended framework TikZ figure with synthesis loop, table comparing static vs. dynamic invariant performance, and discussion of convergence properties.
